newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson deal seen driven by cost savings.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson deal seen driven by cost savings.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson and Co's $6 billion bid for Great Western Financial Corp is driven by huge cost savings that would result from a merger of the two biggest U.S. thrift institutions, analysts said.
"This is a very positive transaction for Ahmanson in that elimination of overlapping branches would drive considerable cost savings," said Morgan Stanley & Co analyst Kenneth Posner.
Ahmanson projected cost savings from the merger at more than $400 million annually.
Arbitrageurs said Great Western was probably shopping for an investment banker to advise it, and possibly was trying to line up a "white knight" to rescue it from Ahmanson.

A Wall Street arbitrageur said he did not think antitrust issues would be a stumbling block to an Ahmanson-Great Western deal. He said regulators generally look at deposit concentrations in specfic communities served by merging financial institutions.
Great Western has assets of about $43 billion, while Ahmanson is larger with about $50 billion. Both are based in California.

Some arbitrageurs were betting that Washington Mutual Savings Bank would emerge as Great Western's white knight. Washington Mutual is a huge Seattle-based thrift that has been an acquirer in the latest wave of consolidation in financial services.

Ahmanson's announcement of its offer had all the earmarks of a hostile bid. Chairman and Chief Executive Charles Rinehart said on CNBC that he had spoken to Great Western Chief Executive John Maher Monday night and that Maher had been surprised to hear of the bid. According to Rinehart, Maher said he wanted time to talk to his board of directors.
Ahmanson said the merger would use purchase accounting, which results in goodwill that must be amortized and subtracted from net income.
The purchase method of accounting, once rarely used in mergers of financial companies, began to come into prominence in 1996.

In the recent wave of thrift consolidations on the U.S. West Coast, Washington Mutual has made a series of acquisitions and San Francisco-based First Nationwide Holdings Inc has acquired Cal Fed Bancorp.
In a statement, Great Western said it would respond to Ahmanson after it had had an opportunity to fully review the offer and consult its advisers.
Great Western was up 9-1/8 to 43-3/8 at midday Tuesday. Ahmanson was up 3-1/2 to 44.
